'''Penelope Evelyn Haxell''' is a Canadian mathematician who works as a professor in the department of combinatorics and optimization at the [[University of Waterloo]]. Her research interests include [[extremal combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/combinatorics-and-optimization/people-profiles/penny-haxell|title=Penny Haxell|work=Combinatorics and Optimization people profiles|publisher=University of Waterloo|accessdate=September 13, 2015|date=April 14, 2015}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Haxell earned a bachelor's degree in 1988 from the University of Waterloo, and completed a doctorate in 1993 from the [[University of Cambridge]] under the supervision of [[Béla Bollobás]].<ref name="kn"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=70416}}</ref> Since then, she has worked at the University of Waterloo, where she was promoted to full professor in 2004.<ref name="kn"/>

==Research==
Haxell's research accomplishments include results on the [[Szemerédi regularity lemma]], [[hypergraph]] generalizations of [[Hall's marriage theorem]] (see [[Haxell's matching theorem]]), [[Linear programming relaxation|fractional]] graph [[packing problems]], and [[strong coloring]] of graphs.<ref name="kn"/>

==Recognition==
Haxell was the 2006 winner of the [[Krieger–Nelson Prize]] of the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]].<ref name="kn">{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2005/res-prizes.html|title=Four honoured for outstanding research achievements|publisher=[[Canadian Mathematical Society]]|date=May 3, 2005|accessdate=September 13, 2015|archive-date=September 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911204639/https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2005/res-prizes.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref>
